title: Puff stitch — the soft rounded bloom
subtitle: Extended half trebles pulled together at the top into a gentle mound
excerpt: Puff stitch is three or more elongated half trebles worked into the same base stitch and drawn together at the top. Softer and more rounded than a bobble, it suits flowery motifs, baby blankets, and any texture that needs a gentle rather than sharp relief.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Vol. 6 (1891) — gathered stitch techniques. The modern puff stitch as a half-treble based cluster is a 20th-century convention built on Victorian cluster traditions.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cluster of elongated half trebles worked into the same base stitch and drawn together at the top. Produces a soft rounded mound on the surface. Sometimes called a puff or a bean stitch.

heroPrompt: A swatch of puff stitch in soft pale pink DK cotton, showing several rounded puff clusters in a grid pattern against a flat dc background, close-up on a cream linen surface, daylight.

inlineDiagramTopics.description: Multiple elongated loops on the hook before the closing pull-through

content.text: uses elongated half trebles pulled up taller than usual. Instead of working them to the standard htr height, you draw each loop up to roughly the height of a treble, creating tall open loops on the hook. All loops are drawn through at once at the end, gathering into a soft rounded mound. The result is gentler than a bobble and doesn't have the sharp-edged quality of a popcorn.
Work to the base stitch where the puff goes.
Yarn over, insert hook into the base stitch, yarn over and pull up a loop — but pull it taller than usual, to treble height. Two elongated loops on the hook.
Yarn over, insert into the same base stitch, pull up another tall loop. Four loops on the hook.
Repeat once more — six loops on the hook (one loop plus three elongated pairs).
Yarn over and pull through all six loops at once.
One chain to close the puff (most patterns require this to keep the top neat). One puff made.

attrs.title: Adjusting puff size
attrs.body: The size of the puff depends on how many loops you pull up (usually 3-5) and how tall each loop is. A 3-loop puff is flatter and tighter; a 5-loop puff with tall loops gives a full rounded bloom. Most patterns specify the loop count. Pulling loops to a consistent height is the key to even puffs.

items.symptom: Puffs are uneven — some tall, some flat
items.cause: Pulling up loops to different heights
items.fix: Use your index finger as a height guide — hold it above the hook and pull each loop up to touch the finger before moving on. Consistent height gives consistent puffs.

items.cause: Too many loops and pulling through too hard, gathering them at different points
items.fix: Yarn over and pull smoothly through all loops in one movement. A closing chain (ch 1) after the pull-through locks the puff and stops the top spreading.

content.text: Puff stitch clusters worked into a magic ring make a flower motif centre — the puffs radiate outward from the ring like petals. Star stitch uses a similar gather-to-centre method for a star-shaped cluster.
